title.narrative: Emergency support for the early rehabilitation of short-cycle crops production to the food and nutritional security of vulnerable people affected by Hurricane Rafael

description.narrative: Almost 16 days that hurricane Oscar affected Cuba, on 6 November 2024, Category 3 Hurricane Rafael hit the western region of Cuba with maximum sustained winds of 120 to 140 km per hour and significant rains affecting the mainly the provinces of Artemisa, Mayabeque and La Habana. After the impact of Hurricane Rafael, in these provinces it was reported severe damage on the agricultural sector such as more than 6 733 hectares of vegetables, 9 677 hectares of bananas, 4 384 hectares of cassava and 755 hectares of fruits. At least 10 irrigation machines were overturned. The livestock sector suffered from the loss of over 100 000 animals, including starter and laying hens, due to the impact of the winds, rains and the lack of electricity and damaged infrastructures. In total, the roofs of 120 poultry farms, 26 pig farms and 32 dairy farms were afftected. Strong impacts on the pig program, including pig companies with large producers and pork marketers, which also contribute greatly to the feeding of the capital. The impact on food security and nutrition resulted in significant losses in the forecasted production of poultry and pigs. The availability of food in the country was further at risk, threatening the food security of the population.This adds to an already very complex situation due to the total or partial absence of electricity impacting water supply and the potential loss of stored food.According to the magnitude of the damage and losses caused by Hurricane Rafael with negatively impacted on food and nutritional security, not only in the short term, but also in the medium and long term, the project will focus on the rapid rehabilitation of short-cycle crop production in the most affected municipalities of the province of Artemisa (Guira de Melena, Alquízar, Artemisa, San Antonio de los Baños, Mariel, and Guanajay) and Mayabeque (Batabanó and Quivicán). The availability of food is one of the main problems in this area. For this reason, it has been prioritized by the FAO in support to the government. Vegetables become even more important in times of scarcity than other foods left unsatisfied by extensive hurricane damage. That is why the government authorities have prioritized the production of vegetables among other needs to be supported immediately with CERF resources. Main support will be provided for the early rehabilitation of vegetable production of spanish's chard, chinese's chard, lettuce, pepper and tomato. FAO will provide technical assistance to introduce more resilient production practices focused on supporting the immediate resumption of agricultural production that the affected population needs for daily consumption, as part of their regular diet and as a good source of nutrients. This project will contribute to support 7 102 farmers by providing seeds of vegetables and some inputs to increase the production of short-cycle crops by 3,500 ha. FAO activities are aimed at curbing the deteriorating food security situation in the affected communities supporting the sources of local fresh food for the beneficiary population (489,000 beneficiaries).
